content: {"id": "f33d3ea3-7b03-41dc-94fb-31f322cadcb0", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "On a Windows Server 2019 EC2 instance, AWS-RunPatchBaseline fails with 0x80070422 'The service cannot be started' and Get-Service wuauserv shows StartType: Disabled. Why can't SSM just start it, and how do I fix it?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
{"id": "df70e475-37e4-483b-98de-f4c9e6b137b0", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "chat_title", "title": "Windows Update Service Disabled SSM Patch Baseline Failure"}]}

{"id": "1deb2e37-ecbe-450f-92de-b0ad4807a800", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Good question — this is a classic SSM-vs-Windows-Update-Agent conflict. Let me explain why SSM can't just start it, then give you the fix.

## Why SSM can't just start wuauserv itself

AWS-RunPatchBaseline (and the underlying patch manager) relies on the native Windows Update Agent (`wuauserv`) to actually scan/install updates on Windows Server. It doesn't bundle its own patching engine for Windows — it drives the OS-native one.

The error `0x80070422` is the standard Win32 "The service cannot be started, either because it is disabled or because it has no enabled devices associated with it" — this is Windows itself refusing the start request, not an SSM permissions or agent issue. SSM Agent runs as SYSTEM and has full rights to start services, but **Windows Service Control Manager enforces StartType at the OS level** — if a service's StartType is `Disabled`, SCM will reject *any* start request regardless of who's asking, SYSTEM included. SSM would have to explicitly re-enable the service first, and the document doesn't do that automatically because disabling `wuauserv` is usually a deliberate hardening/policy action (common in CIS/STIG baselines, or GPO-managed environments that push updates another way, e.g. WSUS/SCCM) — SSM won't silently override an intentional security posture without being told to.

So the chain is: GPO or local policy sets `wuauserv` Start to `4` (Disabled) → SCM blocks starts → RunPatchBaseline's attempt to start the service fails → 0x80070422.

## The fix

**1. Set the service back to enabled (Manual is the standard/expected StartType for wuauserv):**
```powershell
Set-Service -Name wuauserv -StartupType Manual
Start-Service -Name wuauserv
Get-Service wuauserv | Select-Object Status, StartType
```

**2. Check for a GPO/registry override that's re-disabling it** — if it's policy-managed, your PowerShell fix will get reverted on the next GPO refresh. Check:
```powershell
Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
```
Look for `NoAutoUpdate` or any policy forcing WSUS. If this instance is meant to use WSUS/SCCM instead of SSM Patch Manager, that's a design decision to resolve (pick one patching source), not just a service flag to flip.

**3. If it's set via local policy only (not domain GPO):**
Run `gpedit.msc` → Computer Configuration → Administrative Templates → Windows Components → Windows Update, and check nothing there forces it off — or just confirm no `Services\wuauserv\Start` registry override exists at `HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\wuauserv`.

**4. Re-run RunPatchBaseline** once the service holds at Manual/Enabled across a reboot or policy refresh.

If you're managing this at scale, it's worth automating the `Set-Service` fix via an SSM document or State Manager association that runs before RunPatchBaseline, so new instances don't drift back to Disabled.

Want me to check whether this instance has an SSM association or patch baseline configured, or look at its recent command history for this document?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
